description: Rice blast is one of the most destructive diseases of rice worldwide. The fungus infects leaves, nodes, and panicles. On leaves it produces characteristic diamond-shaped lesions that reduce photosynthesis and weaken the plant.
symptoms: Diamond or spindle-shaped lesions on leaves
Lesions with gray or white center and brown or reddish border
Small spots that enlarge and merge on leaves
Leaf drying or death in severe infections
In severe cases young plants may die
visual_symptoms: gray or white center with brown border
favorable_conditions: Long periods of leaf wetness (dew, rain, fog)
disease_cycle: Fungus survives on infected seeds and crop residues
Spores are produced on infected tissues
Spores spread by wind or water
Infection occurs when leaves remain wet
New lesions produce more spores causing rapid disease cycles
impact: Severe outbreaks can cause major crop losses
biological_control: Use beneficial microbes such as Trichoderma species
prevention: Regular field monitoring for early symptoms
source: Plant pathology references on rice blast
